Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:10:1.hebrew: הקדישו מוקדש - לאו קדוש ממש, אלא ליתן דבר מועט בפדיונו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:10:1.english: [If] he consecrated it, [it is] consecrated - [It is] not actually consecrated; rather, [he is required] to give a small amount for its redemption.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:10:2.hebrew: כדרבי אבהו - דאמר במסכת ערכין (דף כג:) גבי מקדיש נכסיו והיתה עליו כתובת אשה ובעל חוב, וקתני התם דיהיב להקדש מידי פורתא וגבי בעל חוב דיליה. ואמר ר' אבהו דהא דבעי למיתב להקדש מידי, משום גזירה שמא יאמרו הקדש גמור יוצא לחולין בלא פדיון:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:10:2.english: Like [that of] Rabbi Abbahu - As he said in Tractate Arakhin (23b) regarding one who consecrates his property while he had a woman's marriage contract and a creditor [claiming] against him, and it is taught there that one gives a small amount to the Temple treasury and the creditor collects his [debt]. And Rabbi Abbahu said that the reason one must give something to the Temple treasury [is] because of a decree, lest [people] say [that] fully consecrated property goes out to non-sacred status without redemption.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:11:1.english: [If] he sold it, it is sold - [The Gemara] explains this entire baraita below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:11:2.english: Once he stood trial - [The ox's] body became liened to the injured party, and it is his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:11:4.english: It is not sold - And even for plowing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:11:5.english: [If] he consecrated it, it is not consecrated - And he does not even give anything to the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:12:1.english: [If] creditors came first, etc. - [The Gemara] explains the reason below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:13:1.english: [If] he sold it, [it is] sold - [This] refers to an innocuous ox before it stood trial.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:15:1.english: In accordance with [the statement of] Rabbi Abbahu - that he gives a small amount.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:16:1.english: He gave it as a gift, what he did is done, for plowing - Like a sale.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:16:2.hebrew: אלא שחטו - קס"ד מה שעשה עשוי לאפקועי מניזק קאמר, דהתם ליכא למימר לרדיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:16:2.english: But [if] he slaughtered it - [The Gemara] initially assumed that [the phrase] "what he did is done" means to remove [the ox] from the injured party['s claim], for there one cannot say [that it refers to using it] for plowing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:16:3.english: [If] he gave it as a gift, what he did is done, for plowing - [It is] like a sale.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:18:1.hebrew: לפחת שחיטה - מה שנפחתו דמיו בשחיטתו, אין המזיק משלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:18:1.english: To the depreciation of slaughter - That which its value depreciated through its slaughter, the damager does not pay.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:19:1.english: Another’s lien - Land that is mortgaged to another.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:1:1.hebrew: כיון דמשעבד ליה - דאי לא יהיב ליה דמי, שקיל ליה לשור, דרחמנא שעבדיה ניהליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:1:1.english: Since it is liened to him - For if he does not give him money, he takes the ox, for the Merciful One [the Torah] liened it to him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:20:1.english: Obvious - For from here we learn it without the statement of Rav Huna.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:21:1.hebrew: ה"ג הא נמי רבה אמרה דאמר רבה - רבה אדם חשוב היה, ומאדם חשוב — כגון רב או רבה — פרכינן כאילו כתיב במשנה או בברייתא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:21:1.english: This is the reading: Rabba stated this as well, as Rabba says - Rabba was an eminent person, and from an eminent person — such as Rav or Rabba — we raise an objection as though it were written in a Mishnah or in a Baraita.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:22:1.english: [It] is like one who dug pits, ditches, or caves in it - For the slaughter is visible and discernible.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:23:1.english: Whether [it] caused damage before he owed - before its owner borrowed the money from the creditors.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:2:1.hebrew: והתניא מכרו מכור - אמר ליה, חוזר וגובהו ניזק מלוקח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:2:1.english: But isn't it taught: [If] he sold it, [it is] sold - He [Rav Nachman] said to him [Rava]: The injured party returns and collects it from the purchaser.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:2:2.hebrew: לרידיא - שאם חרש בו לוקח, אינו נותן דמי החרישה לניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:2:2.english: For plowing - [Meaning] that if the buyer plowed with it, he does not pay the value of the plowing to the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:3:1.hebrew: ש"מ - בתמיה, והא מטלטלין לאו מידי דקאי בעיניה ולא סמיך מלוה עלייהו, ואמאי טרפינן להו מלוקח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:3:1.english: Conclude from this - [This is asked] in astonishment: for movable property is not something that remains intact, and a lender does not rely upon it, so why would we seize it from a buyer?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:3:2.english: Designated payment [apotiki] - The Merciful One rendered it [designated] to collect from this ox.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:4:1.english: The creditor does not collect from it - And here, why does [the injured party] collect it from the purchaser?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:5:1.hebrew: ומשני עבד טעמא מאי - גובהו מלוקח, משום דאית ליה קלא לשעבודיה כי שווי' אפותיקי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:5:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: What is the reason [regarding] a slave - [that] he collects him from a purchaser? Because his lien has publicity when he makes him an apotiki [designated repayment].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:6:1.english: From the West - He was from the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:8:1.hebrew: מכרו אינו מכור - קס"ד אפי' לרדיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:8:1.english: If he sold it, it is not sold - It was initially assumed [that this applies] even [if he sold it] for plowing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:9:1.hebrew: לעולם מזיק - ומכרו אינו מכור לגופיה קאמר, דהדר גבי ליה, ואפילו לרבי ישמעאל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 33b:9:1.english: Actually, [it is] the one liable for the damage - And "he sold it, it is not sold" means with respect to [the ox] itself, for [the injured party] goes back and collects it, and [this applies] even according to Rabbi Yishmael.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:15:1.hebrew: משום דרבי אבהו - אבל בלא ר' אבהו לא קדיש, משום דקדושת דמים אין מפקעת מידי שעבוד. ומיירי הכא בבעל מום, א"נ בתם, וכגון שהקדישו לבדק הבית דקדוש קדושת דמים, וכדאמרינן (תמורה דף ו.): "המתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית — מה שעשה עשוי". וקשה מכאן לר"ת, שמפרש דבכל קדושת מטלטלין מפקעת מידי שעבוד, ואפי' קדושת דמים. ואומר ר"ת דאלמוה רבנן לשעבודא דניזק, כדאמרינן בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא צ. ושם): "אלמוה רבנן לשעבודיה דבעל":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:15:1.english: "Due to Rabbi Abbahu" - But without [the enactment of] Rabbi Abbahu it would not be consecrated, because monetary sanctity [kedushat damim] does not release [an item] from a lien. And here [the Gemara] is dealing with a blemished [animal], or alternatively with an unblemished [animal], such as where he consecrated it for the upkeep of the Temple [bedek habayit], which is consecrated [only] with monetary sanctity, as we say (Temurah 6a): "One who consecrates unblemished [animals] for the upkeep of the Temple — what he has done is done [i.e., valid]." And this poses a difficulty for Rabbeinu Tam, who explains that in all [cases of] consecration of movable property, it releases [the item] from a lien, even monetary sanctity. And Rabbeinu Tam says that the Rabbis strengthened the lien of the injured party, just as we say in [the chapter] HaChovel (below, Bava Kamma 90a, and there): "The Rabbis strengthened the lien of the husband."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:19:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת המזיק שעבודו של חבירו פטור - ופליג אדרשב"ג דמחייב בהשולח (גיטין מא. ושם) לחד מאמוראי דהתם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:19:1.english: "That is to say, one who causes damage to another's liened property is exempt" - And [Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua] disagrees with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who holds [him] liable in [Chapter] HaShole'ach (Gittin 41a, and [the references] there), according to one of the Amoraim there.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:19:2.hebrew: שמע מינה ב"ח מאוחר שקדם וגבה כו' - ודלא כבן ננס בפרק מי שהיה נשוי (כתובות דף צד.), דלדידיה כי היכי דבקרקעות עדיף ב"ח מאוחר משום נעילת דלת טפי מלוקח מאוחר, הכי נמי אע"ג דמלוקח מאוחר גבי ליה ניזק — כדאמר לעיל, משום דאית ליה קלא — מב"ח מאוחר לא גבי ליה משום נעילת דלת:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 33b:19:2.english: Infer from this [that] a later creditor who went ahead and collected [his debt], etc. - And [this is] not in accordance with Ben Nannas in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehayah Nasui (Ketubot 94a), for according to him, just as with respect to land a later creditor has an advantage over a later purchaser because of [the concern of] "locking the door" [against borrowers], so too, even though the injured party collects [it] from a later purchaser — as [the Gemara] stated above, because it has publicity — he does not collect [it] from a later creditor because of [the concern of] "locking the door."
